MDR-TB patients:2012
================
PMDT R&R system has been revised since the previous one was not successful. The revised system was started in Thailand fiscal year of 2012. Given some delays for laboratory results of second-line DST, the detection (Number of new and previous treated cases with available DST results)and enrolment (Number of M/XDR-TB patients started treatment)are available 12-15 months later. Thus, detection & enrolment of TB patients under the DOTS program in 2012 will be available at the end of 2013.

Drug resistance surveillance:2012
================
(1) Routine lab request does not include patient information such as age, sex and HIV status. These results were from National reference laboratory at central level only. Data from other laboratories providing culture and DST are not routinely reported to NTP.
(2) Patients of 2.25 were registered in the DOTS program from both 2011 (the last two quaters) and 2012. However, their sputum samples were performed culture & DST in 2012.

Treatment outcomes:2011
==================
(1) Last year, Thailand reported TB case notification in 2011 as 65,824. However, treatment outcome was available for 51,782. This is mainly due to a)EP of 10,014 cases were not routinely reported for treatment outcome. In addition, some private hospitals reported TB case notification but did not submit treatment outcome. (2)item 2.39 includes only new smear-negative patients because routine reporting system does not collect treatment outcomes of EP or smear not done/unknown.

Treatment outcomes (HIV+ cases):2011
================

Treatment outcomes (MDR-TB and XDR-TB cases):2010
================
Routine MDR-TB reports started in 2009 were not quite successful. Very few hospitals (5%) submitted all MDR-TB reports to NTP because the forms had been changed frequently and no supervisions were conducted at practice level. After the GLC monitoring mission in October 2012, the PMDT records and reports have been revised. First quarter of 2012 (1 Oct-31 Dec 2011)was started of the revised system. Thus, data before 1 October 2011 (Thailand fiscal year) were not collected.

TB infection control:2012
================
Routine report system does not collect these data (3.11 & 3.12).

Public-Private and Public-Public Mix (PPM):2012

remarks.general:
Questions 2.1 New smear positive pulmonary TB cases notified increased significantly in 2009 (1206) compared to 2008 (867). There does not appear to have been an increase in diagnostic laboratories or greater involvement of the non-public sector providers. Please provide comments on why such a significant increase occurred in 2009? 

Answer: The NSP notification in 2008 and first quarter 2009 was very low due to poor quality Carbol Fuschin used at the microscopy centers. The stocks of CF were replaced by GDF and there after the NSP cases detection went up. The other reason was intensive training of Laboratory technicians on smear microscopy undertaken in early 2009. Together these steps improve NSP case notification. 

Questions 2.2 New smear negative pulmonary TB cases notified increased significantly in 2009 (3095) compared to 2008 (1996). There does not appear to have been an increase in diagnostic services, health facilities or greater involvement of the non-public sector providers. Please provide comments on why such a significant increase occurred in 2009? 

Answer: There has been no increase in diagnostics services for detection of smear negative cases. A large number of expatriate doctors (mostly Cuban doctors and some other nationalities) and some local doctors in spite of having had training on NTP guidelines continue to rely unduly on x-ray. This over reliance was also been amplified due to poor quality of microscopy in earlier years. NTP has been focusing on case finding in general and this added impetus to case finding has resulted in increase in both new smear positive as well negative cases.  


In addition the ratio of new smear negative PTB cases : new smear positive PTB cases in 2009 increased to 2.5:1 from 2.3:1 in 2008. Please provide comments on why this ratio has increased even further in favour of smear negative PTB cases? 

Answer: The above two explanations add upto explaining this point. The ratio of smear negative to positive still remains high mainly as large numbers of public doctors particularly in the referral and tertiary hospitals do not follow the NTP diagnostic algorithms. They continue to rely on x-ray and also they have a low opinion of quality of smear microscopy at the facility level. At the community health centers there is low referral of TB suspects for microscopy. The NTP is addressing these issues by organizing regular training and sensitization of doctors in the country, sensitization of the medical association and coordination with the Cuban Doctors Brigade that provide doctors at the CHC level.

Q 2.20: could you please confirm the big increase from 2008 to 2009? 
Response: In 2008 referral from TB facilities to VCCT had not been started in the country. In 2009 two facilities initiated referral of TB patients for to VCCT centres within the health facility. They refereed 108 TB patients for counseling and testing. Only documented referrals have been reported. There were other referrals as well but such information was not well documented and therefore has not been included in the data reported.

Q 2.24: 100 patients registered HIV+ (whatever year of diagnosis) were reported last year. Could you explain the decline seen in 2009?  
Response: There was an error. In 2009 a total of 151 HIV cases were registered of which 51 new cases were diagnosed in 2009. 

Q 2.27: could you clarify with HIV programme the number of HIV patients with TB on ART and TB treatment as zero is reported by TB programme in 2.23? 
Response: The information in 2.23 is a subset of 2.20 and 2.21 for which the TB programme has documentation. Among the 108 TB patients who were referred to VCTC center none had been found to be HIV positive.

remarks.general:
The TB program in Timor-Leste is supported by The Global Fund for AIDS, TB and Malaria. Program costs are borne by The Global Fund. Domestic Funds support infrastructure, staffs, consumables and advocacy related activities.

Diagnosis , Treatment, Monitoring and Evaluation is supported through The Global Fund.

DOTS in Timor-Leste is implemented through Community Volunteers (Promoter Saude Familia or Family Health Volunteers)at the basic health post (lowest level of health care infrastructure), health staff, NGOs staffs and faith based organization.

Some Salient Program Features/Activities/ Achievements:
1. DST is currently not available in Timor-Leste.
2. The first ever DRS survey is planned in 2018.
3. All MDR-TB Cases are treated as in patients with a long regimen of 20 months. Plans are to introduce the shorter regimen of 9-12 months in 2018.
4. Detection of MDR-TB cases are low, on an average 2-6 cases are detected per year against an estimated 30-60 MDR-TB cases.
5. 83% families burdened with catastrophic costs of TB (Survey done in 2016-17).
6. Systematic screening of TB suspects is being piloted in Timor-Leste in 2018.
remarks.sections:
Drug resistance surveillance:2017
================
1. Timor-Leste does not have the facility for second line DST. 
2. No tests are currently being done to detect INH, Fluoroquinolone, 2LI or any other resistance. Only Rifampicin resistance tests using GeneXpert(R) platform is being conducted.

1. Facility for diagnosing XDR-TB is not available in Timor-Leste.

Laboratory diagnostic services:2017

TB infection control:2017

TB preventive therapy:2017
===============================
As per the current guidelines on IPT in Timor-Leste, children under five years are put in treatment if any of the household contacts are suffering from bacteriologically confirmed TB. The data collected is part of routine surveillance system. However, the IPT data on adults and adolescents are not available. 

Palliative care:2017
======================
No patients were given oral morphine

Services utilisation:2017
=====================
1. All MDR-TB Patients are treated as indoor patients so 100% are hospitalized in a specialized centre Klibur Domin (Tibar)
2. Hospitalization details for TB patients are not collect by the routine data collection system in Timor-Leste. The estimates provided are based on anecdotal evidence from Klibur Domin
3. On an average, for first line TB patients, the number of visits to a health facility is 2 (Diagnosis) + 3 subsequent (Months 2, 4 and 6. DOT is provided by Community Volunteers

The program is fully supported by The Global Fund grant for the period 2018-2020.

Programs that do charge do so on a sliding scale and if 3rd party coverage can be captured most program attempt to do so. Our NTP does not directly provide diagnostic evaluation; we support such activities and interventions through our cooperative agreement awards to states and local TB programs.

**********FOLLOW-UP QUESTIONS, OCTOBER 2009*****************************
2.6-2.10 According to your first remark and question 2.25, you have differentiation between new and retreatment cases. Please explain why there are no retreatment cases listed under 2.6-2.10. In addition, please only fill in 0 where the known value is actually 0. Data not available should be left blank. 
In our data collection system, a case of TB within 12 months of previous diagnosis and treatment is not considered a separate case. Therefore we do not collect “relapse” data or treatment after failure or default. As per our first remark, we collect information on previous cases of TB (not within the same 12 month period) and this is what we provided as our definition of “retreatment” for question 2.25.

2.12 This question refers to foreign-born individuals (or non-citizens), not to the classification of new or retreatment. Please revise if necessary. 
This is our total count of foreign-born cases for 2008 (n = 7563).

2.18-2.26: there seem to be some slight discrepancies. The total of new (8868) and previously diagnosed (408) is less than the total given at 2.18. 
Unknown/missing = 89
The total of cases with MDR (103) is less than the total of new (83) and previously diagnosed (17) as reported separately. Were there some cases with previous history unknown? 
This has been corrected; new MDR n = 86.
It also seems strange that only 1 of the 103 MDR cases is reported to have been started on treatment with SLDs (2.20). 
This has been updated to n=14. Our surveillance system captures initial drug regimens, which do not usually include SLD treatment unless there is reason to believe the patient has MDR-TB. Ultimately these 103 MDR patients are treated appropriately but our current surveillance system reflects their initial regimen.
Why were only 65 of 103 cases tested for resistance to SLDs? Please clarify. 
The SLD testing information submitted for 2008 is comparable to past year’s submissions (in last year’s submission n=69 for this question item). Our dataset is dynamic; testing is not complete for all cases at the end of our data cycle

3.8 The years in this question refer to the year the assessment was done (rather than the year the data refer to). Please revise. 
These represent our most recent data and the year that we next anticipate data.

remarks.general:
Preguntas 2,38 - 2,39 - 2,40.- 
Respecto a la diferencia en las cifra final de los pacientes evaluados de la cohorte del 2007, esta se debe a que en el Informe Trimestral enviado por las provincias, solo recoge la información de los casos pulmonares con confirmación bacteriológica y mayores de quince años; el resto, son evaluados clínicamente.

Pregunta 2,39.-
con respecto a la diferencia en las cifras finales de los pacientes evaluados de la cohorte del 2007 en el grupo de otros casos nuevos no incluidos en los casos pulmonares con baciloscopia positiva o pulmonares con baciloscopia negativa y Extrapulmonares, se incluyeron 133 pacientes con tuberculosis pulmonar con baciloscopia negativa y cultivo positivo.

Pregunta 2,42.- 
Respecto a los casos de retratamiento, los Informes Trimestrales enviados por las provincias recoge la información de la evaluación de la cohorte de Recaídas; la información correspondiente a las Recuperaciones de Abandono a pesar de ser evaluados clínicamente no se envía.
Los pacientes con fracaso de tratamiento correspondieron a casos resistentes a los cuales se les administro el esquema de segunda línea.

Pregunta 3,18.-
Respecto al tratamiento utilizado en los pacientes con recaídas y recuperaciones de abandono, se emplea el mismo esquema para tratar a los casos nuevos (2(HRZE)5/4(HR)3) 

Pregunta 3,25.-
Se realizo un estudio conjunto con la dirección de Epidemiología en el año 2006, se prevé realizar uno similar en el 2010

Pregunta 3,27.-
La respuesta fue NO porque lo que realizamos de rutina a los pacientes con TB son las pruebas de VIH y esta opción no aparece en la pregunta 3,28.

Pregunta 3,29.-
Se coloco NO porque en realidad no se ha realizado una actividad específica de TB Drogoresistente en el 2008; dentro del Curso Técnico Administrativo de Control de la TB se dedican dos días para multidrogoresistencia, mientras en el año 2007 el Dr. Caminero vino al país y dicto un curso para manejo de la TB-MDR a médicos especialistas.

Pregunta 3,40.- 
La respuesta es NO porque durante el año 2008 hubo cambio de autoridades a nivel del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud por lo cual no se contaba con un plan nacional de recursos humanos en salud.

Pregunta 4,40 - 4,43.-
Respecto a la utilización de los servicios de salud: los porcentajes de hospitalización han variado ya que durante este año aumento el número de casos de TB con alcoholismo y diabetes que aumenta la estancia hospitalaria. 

 4: Financiación 

Pregunta 4,13.-
El presupuesto para medicamentos de segunda línea incluye los casos nuevos(25) mas los casos que se arrastran del año anterior(esquema mínimo de 21 meses), y se calcula una reserva del 20%.

Pregunta 4,10.-
No comprendemos la pregunta ya que en el 2007 no se incluyo el presupuesto para la estrategia PAL.

Pregunta 4,25.-
No se incluyo el presupuesto del 2010 para medicamentos de primera línea motivado a que este año se inauguro una planta de Servicios de elaboración de productos farmacéuticos que producirá medicamentos esenciales, dentro de los cuales están los medicamentos de primera línea, sólidos no estériles.
Respecto al presupuesto para medicamentos de primera línea del año 2009, el mismo es mas elevado debido a que se compraron medicamentos con combinaciones a dosis fijas y dispersables, tanto pediátricos como de adultos. Así mismo se incluyo la reserva del 20%.

4.14: Under this budget line, the NTP plans to conduct some interventions such as: develop Community Strategy on TB elimination; revise ACSM/Communication Strategy; Ensure that the Health system legal and regulatory frameworks are in place for expanded services; Ensure an enabling environment for the inclusion of comprehensive TB service and systems within the package of care under Health Insurance; Support the ongoing training of health care providers at all levels in TB prevention and control; Support the ongoing reforms in Preventive medicine to ensure comprehensive TB care services are universally available; Implement the multisectoral accountability framework with time bound targets, etc. 

4.4: In 2021, the NTP has allocated more fund for lab infrastructure, equipment and supplies because we will continue to focus on active case finding using 2X strategy (Xray – Xpert). Therefore, lab infrastructure will be upgraded, more equipment and supplies (ie: mobile Xray car, Xpert machine, Xpert test, etc.) will be purchased for implementation. 

4.7: In 2021, the NTP has allocated more fund for Drug-susceptible TB: programme costs because we want to detect more TB patients. Therefore, targeted actions will be taken to reach all high risk populations, especially children, elderly, PLWH, DM, Poor, smokers, miners, populations in prisons/ houses for social support and other congregate settings. Other interventions will also be conducted in this period, such as:  Intensified case finding in all PHC facilities by introducing systematic screening and referral; Define and deliver a package for intensified case finding in high volume facilities using the FAST approach; Broaden engagement to include Family Medicine Practitioners; Integrate TB into existing models of care including mental health and PAL/PAM; etc.

4.14: In 2021, the NTP plans to conduct more interventions than in previous period such as: develop Community Strategy on TB elimination; revise ACSM/Communication Strategy; Ensure that the Health system legal and regulatory frameworks are in place for expanded services; Ensure an enabling environment for the inclusion of comprehensive TB service and systems within the package of care under Health Insurance; Support the ongoing training of health care providers at all levels in TB prevention and control; Support the ongoing reforms in Preventive medicine to ensure comprehensive TB care services are universally available; Implement the multisectoral accountability framework with time bound targets, etc. 

4.15: In order to achieve the goal of ending TB in Vietnam by 2030, the NTP plans to conduct more interventions/ activities, purchase more TB/ MDR-TB/ LTBI drugs/ equipment/ supplies, apply latest TB detection and diagnosis techniques, etc. Therefore, total budget required in 2021 is higher than total budget required in 2020.

remarks.general:
Vanuatu is a medium TB burden country with the estimated incidence declining from 110 per 100,000 in 2000 to 51 per 100,000 population in 2017 (Global TB report 2018).  The overall treatment coverage is estimated at 65% but of those detected and treated the treatment success rate has been reasonably good at 88%. 
With the detection of 5 cases of RR-TB since March 2017, there has been increased concern within the country on TB control and in response the National TB programme (NTP) requested support to further assess the situation and make recommendations that particularly relate to strengthening the management of TB and DR-TB cases and their contacts.A visit from rGl committee visited the country as well as conducted clinician training.
Case detection is still something the country need to reach it's yearly target.	
Preventive treatment should be strengthened using treatment partners to ensure good adherence as well as data management moving away from paper based to electronic based, however there is still challenges in some areas where there is poor network coverage.

Acknowledge the Funding support from WHO,GF(UNDP, DFAT and Vanuatu government towards the TB Program in Vanuatu.

remarks.general:
The Samoa National TB programme is a collaborative effort of all partners of the Health Sector working together to keep TB at bay. The financial assistance rendered by the WHO and UNDP Global Fund to fight HIV/TB expanded our reach out into the communities and to all other subpopulations never been reached before.

It is anticipated that with strong commitment from the Health Sector and its partners in ensuring the COVID19 does not reach Samoa, it is the same sentiments echoed in trying to keep TB as well as other health issues on top of our agenda as with COVID19. The onus of all the community engagements is to make our people aware of the profound negative impacts of COVID19 on the health of those with already existing health conditions. It is also a call for our people with TB to get their COVID19 vaccine while they have the time and not to wait until the last minute.

TB although a traditional public health issue, but one that cannot be disregarded at this time. Global pandemics interrupt our efforts to combat many other health problems and we must not be complacent at any time at all.

remarks.general:
2.1 	SHARP DECLINE IN BACTERIOLOGICALLY CONFIRMED PULMONARY TB CASES.
Amended
There has been a decline in the smear positive PTB over the years, which is attributable to sensitivity of smear microscopy in HIV positive individuals/ those with paucibacillary disease. In 2011, this was 129 770, 119 898 in 2012 and 109 630 in 2013.
The data reported is still on “new smear positive PTB” (as per guidance provided) despite the fact that Xpert is widely used because;
- Full roll out was attained in October 2013
- The revised data collection tools (paper registers and Electronic TB register) 
  incorporating Xpert were not widely used in 2013.  
- Xpert is used as first line test for all people with symptoms and smear  
  microscopy is conducted on people with Xpert positive Rif susceptible results 
  only. Since some of the Xpert positive are smear negative, others smears were 
  not done, they are not included in the bacteriologically confirmed. 
- Xpert was not used for extra pulmonary specimens in 2013
The total MTB detected Rif susceptible (laboratory confirmed) = 187 990
This will be better reflected in 2014 data as we will be in a position to include all Xpert diagnosed patients in bacteriologically confirmed. 

2.10	SUBSTANTIAL DROP IN THE NUMBER OF LAB CONFIRMED MDR-TB CASES COMPARED TO PREVIOUS YEARS 
This is an area of investigation; the laboratory data is incomplete for both MDR-TB and XDR-TB. The NHLS has been in the process of rolling out a new information system it is not clear at this stage whether this could have contributed to this.
It is definitely not a result of de duplication of laboratory data. The data will be updated once the problem has been identified and resolved.

2.11	NUMBER IS CLOSE TO THE ONE IN 2.10
Amended 
The number of RR-TB unconfirmed as MDR-TB is 3 344 
	
2.26(a)	FINAL NUMBER OF HIV POSITIVE TB PATIENTS ON ART IN 2012 LESS THAN THE PROVISIONAL NUMBER REPORTED LAST YEAR.
Amended
The final number of TB patients started on ART in 2012 is 101 937

2.26(b)	COLLABORATE WITH COLLEAGUES IN THE NATIONAL AIDS PROGRAMME TO ENSURE ONE FIGURE IS REPORTED NATIONALLY FOR HIV POSITIVE TB ON ART DURING 2013
Noted, the different reporting times still pose a challenge.

2.30	TREATMENT OUTCOME OF 354 270 NEW AND RELAPSE CASES REPORTED AGAINST 323 664 SUCH CASES REPORTED LAST YEAR.
Amended
The treatment outcomes for All New and Relapse cases in 2012 are reported for 328 393 patients. This is against the 323 664 All new and relapse cases reported in the 2012 notifications. The variance of 4 729 cases is due to updated data by provinces after the reporting period.

2.31	TREATMENT OUTCOMES OF 327 816 PREVIOUSLY TREATED CASES IS BEING REPORTED AGAINST 25 918 SUCH CASES REPORTED LAST YEAR.	
Amended
41 patients were not evaluated which brings the total number of patients not evaluated to 2330
The number of HIV positive TB patients was reported as 190 093 in 2012, this was updated to 200 012

2.33(a)	WHY DO 42% OF MDR-TB CASES HAVE NO OUTCOMES REPORTED?
Data amended
The high rate of "not evaluated" is due to incomplete data and reporting by provinces. This is currently done manually and has posed challenges for high case load facilities. We are still working on the MDR and XDR-TB data and the outcomes will be updated in the 2015 report

2.33(b)	WHY IS THE SIZE OF THE COHORT BIGGER THAN THE NUMBER OF CASES REPORTED TO HAVE STARTED TREATMENT IN 2011? 
In 2011 there were 11 759 RR-TB and MDR-TB laboratory confirmed patients in total. Of these, only 5 643 were started on treatment. The total number of confirmed RR-TB and MDR-TB cases started on treatment was updated after the reporting period.This data was not updated in the 2013 report.   

2.33(c)	ARE ALL THESE PATIENTS CONFIRMED RR-TB/ MDR-TB?
Yes, as indicated above, the final number of laboratory confirmed RR-TB and MDR-TB started on treatment for 2011 is therefore 6 163.

4.11 The increase in budget for second line medicines is due to the introduction of new medicines for MDR-TB, preXDR and XDR-TB.These are Levofloxacin (children), Moxifloxacin (adults), Clofazimine, Linezoli

Reporting of TB from some provinces is rather poor. Mashonaland Central Province had one district where for the whole of 2008 it was not possible to get a district TB coordinator in 2 of the 8 districts for various reasons. Mavingo province had similar challenges in 2 of 8 provinces. The year 2008 was particulary difficult to function for all the levels because of the tense political climate, the severe macroecenomic crisis which was characterised by record hyper-inflation. Most health facilities were operating at less than 20% of their capacity because health workers were not even able to afford to report for duty regulary.

The 25-44 age group was not disagregated in the old M/E tools.The ME tools have since been revised to ensure that age groups are disagregated.

The M/E tools for HIV have not been revised too capture TB indicators and this process is actually now underway.

Treatment outcomes for HIV positive TB cases were not analyzed separately mainly because more than 80% of our TB cases are HIV positive therefore it did not seem to be necessary to conduct such kind of analysis as it does not add value.
Tracing of contacts is being done but is not being reported on and this will be addressed in future.

A significant number of TB patients receive support from various NGOs in the context of HIV/AIDS mitigation but there is no readily available data on this activity fom NGOs. We shall try to adress this shortcoming in colloboration with the National AIDS Council
